column1: # Correct readings for homograph-set.jsonl. One row per (sentence, form).
# tatoeba_id  form  lemma  pos  cell  labeled_by  checked_by  note
# pos: verb, noun, adj, pron, det, adv, prep, conj, propn, num, intj
# lemma: for a verb, its infinitive without attached pronouns (irse and se
#   fue are ir; arrepentirse, which has no other form, stays); for anything
#   else the dictionary form (noun singular, adjective masculine singular).
# cell: for a verb, the table cell(s) the form fills here, from verbs.json
#   (e.g. indicative.present.3s; several joined with "|" when the sentence
#   cannot tell them apart); empty for other parts of speech.
# labeled_by: who chose the label (e.g. claude-opus-5.5@2026-11-12). Every
#   row was labelled from the sentence, the word and its candidate readings
#   alone, never from gramalysis's answer.
# checked_by: comma-separated reviewers who agreed (model id or "owner"),
#   with the date; a reviewer who disagrees changes the row and says so in
#   the note.
# Conventions (decided for gramalysis; the grammar follows the same ones):
# - A past participle is one form of its verb; its use decides the label.
#   * haber + participle is a compound tense: the verb (he cerrado). The
#     participle after haber never agrees.
#   * ser + participle is the passive: the verb (fue construida, ha sido
#     vendido, será publicado).
#   * estar + participle is a state: an adjective use, labelled adj with the
#     masculine singular as lemma (la puerta está cerrada → cerrado adj). The
#     same for the other linking verbs: quedar(se), parecer, resultar, seguir,
#     andar, sentirse, verse, encontrarse, permanecer.
#   * after a noun: with the verb's own complements (an agent with por,
#     a phrase saying where/when/how the action was done) a participle phrase,
#     the verb (un libro escrito en inglés, una casa construida en 1900);
#     without them an adjective use, adj (una puerta cerrada, agua hervida).
#   * object + participle saying what state the object is in is an adjective
#     use, adj (dejó la puerta abierta, tengo las manos atadas).
#   * a participle phrase opening the sentence (Terminada la cena, salimos)
#     is the verb.
#   * a participle that became a noun is a noun (el pasado, un herido, los
#     abogados). The drifted adjectives in drifted-participles.txt
#     (atrevido, divertido, complicado, conocido…) are adj wherever they are
#     used like an adjective, with ser too (es complicado); after haber they
#     are still the verb (ha complicado).
# - Polite commands: usted is subjunctive.present.3s, ustedes
#   subjunctive.present.3p (hable más despacio); a negative command is the
#   subjunctive (no hables: subjunctive.present.2s); "let's" is
#   subjunctive.present.1p, except a form only the imperative has (vamos:
#   imperative.present.1p). Affirmative tú / vosotros commands are
#   imperative.present.2s / 2p (habla, hablad).
# - ser / ir share fui, fue, fuimos, fueron, fuera, fuese…: ir when it says
#   motion or a destination (fue a Madrid, se fue, fue a ver), ser when it
#   says what something is or was (fue difícil, fue un error, fue construida,
#   la fiesta fue ayer).
# - Accents: the word is read as written; tú/tu, él/el, sí/si, sé/se, dé/de,
#   más/mas, mí/mi, qué/que… are different words. A written accent that is a
#   typo for another word (esta for está) is labelled with the intended word
#   and the note "accent typo"; such rows never become examples.
# - An infinitive is the verb, also with an article (el fumar), except the
#   lexicalised nouns (el deber, el poder, el placer, el amanecer…): noun.
# - lo + participle (lo acordado, lo ocurrido) is an adjective use, adj.
# - hay, había, habrá… (there is) are haber.
